diagnostic_evidence.quote: in which network parameters are learned from data rather than constructed analytically

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and introduction say that grade-wise training, i.e. the greedy per-grade minimisation of the residual loss, provably yields vanishing error. The paper only proves that a specific analytically constructed sequence of affine maps exists. Those maps are hand-built cutoff networks whose first layers carry the input x forward. Nothing shows that the argmin or training procedure of Section 2 reproduces such blocks or has any contraction property. A trained earlier grade need not preserve the structure the construction relies on, so optimality at each grade does not imply the constructed decay. The conclusion itself lists training dynamics as an open problem.

failure_location.quote: To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first rigorous theoretical guarantee that grade-wise training yields provable vanishing approximation error in deep networks.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the abstract and introduction to say the paper proves the existence and explicit construction of a multigrade ReLU scheme with vanishing residuals. Remove or qualify the claim about guarantees for grade-wise training.
issues.overall_effect: The headline interpretation of the results as a guarantee for MGDL training is not established. What is proved is the existence and explicit construction of a multigrade ReLU scheme.
issues.title: Claim of a guarantee for grade-wise training, but only an analytic existence construction is proved
issues.why_classification: Rewording suffices and every formal result stays intact. Only the advertised interpretation is narrowed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The circled $\ReLU$ represents a block of $d$ \ReLU{} units

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:main:mgdl:one:op gives maps A_1..A_n for a network whose first layer reads the input x. In the concatenated MGDL network, the new first layer A_{n_1+1} receives the output of the previous layer ReLU∘A_{n_1}, which is a 5d-vector, not x. The new grades therefore compose with all earlier layers. The proof applies the theorem to f_{n_1+1} as a black box and never argues that the earlier layers carry x forward. That carrying only holds inside the internal construction of Stage I, via d units with ReLU(x)=x on [0,1]^d. The theorem statement does not provide it.

failure_location.quote: Next, apply Theorem~\ref{thm:main:mgdl:one:op} again to $f_{n_1+1}\in C([0,1]^d)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the one-step theorem to a prefix-compatible version: the first affine map may read x from a preceding layer that carries x in d units. Check that the Stage I construction satisfies this, then iterate.
issues.overall_effect: The passage from one-step contraction to the infinite sequence (i)-(ii) of Theorem thm:main:mgdl, and the subsequence of the corollary, is not justified by the theorem as stated.
issues.title: Iterating the one-step theorem ignores that later grades receive the previous layers' output, not x
issues.why_classification: The needed fact is already visible in the Stage I architecture. Stating and verifying a strengthened one-step lemma is a contained new argument, and it leaves the method and conclusions unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary is stated for all ε in (0,1) and says the subsequence k_j is built from the n_i of Theorem thm:main:mgdl:one:op. That theorem and the operator T_ε need ε < 1/(1+2^d). This is needed for the overlap bound 2^d ε M_g ≤ g and for the positivity of 1-ε-2^d ε in the definition of δ. For larger ε the construction is undefined. The corollary's stated range is not proved, and no proof of the corollary is written out.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition of a positive ε-contraction is only the norm inequality ‖g^+ - Tg‖_∞ ≤ (1-ε)‖g^+‖_∞. The proof asserts the pointwise one-sided bounds 0 ≤ g^+ - Tg and 0 ≤ g^- - T(-g). Without them a = g^+ - Tg and b = g^- - T(-g) only satisfy |a|,|b| ≤ (1-ε)‖g‖, so |a-b| can reach 2(1-ε)‖g‖. A counterexample is Tg = g^+ + (1-ε)‖g^+‖φ(g) with φ(g)=1 and φ(-g)=-1 for some g with ‖g^+‖=‖g^-‖=1. Then T is a positive ε-contraction, but ‖g - Sg‖ = 2(1-ε). The lemma as stated is false. The one-sided bound is only established for T_ε (via C1-C2) in the proof of Lemma lem:P1P2:to:positive:eps:constraction.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume C1 and C2 (or the pointwise one-sided estimate 0 ≤ g^+ - Tg ≤ (1-ε)‖g^+‖) in the symmetrization lemma, which T_ε satisfies.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is false as stated. Its use for S_ε is valid only because T_ε additionally satisfies C1-C2.
issues.title: Symmetrization lemma uses a one-sided pointwise bound not implied by the norm-based definition of positive ε-contraction
issues.why_classification: A local change of hypothesis, already verified for T_ε, repairs it. The method and conclusion are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: Here ψ is 1 on [-1,1] and 0 for |x| ≥ r. Ψ(x) = (1/d)Σψ(x_i) equals 1 on [-1,1]^d but is positive whenever a single coordinate satisfies |x_i| < r. For d ≥ 2, Ψ((0,100,...)) ≥ 1/d > 0, so Γ_Q is nonzero far outside rQ and violates the required cutoff property. The proof's steps all rely on localisation: 'Γ=0 outside ∪rQ_i', the bound Σ_iΓ_i ≤ 2^d via bounded overlap, and T_ε g ≤ g^+. Each of these fails. T_ε g can be positive where g<0, and the same failure breaks h_k=0 on Ω_2 (resp. Ω_1) in Stage II. A compactly supported nonzero function cannot be a finite one-hidden-layer ReLU network for d ≥ 2, so a proper cutoff (e.g. σ(Σψ(x_i)-(d-1))) needs an extra hidden layer, which does not fit the one-ReLU-layer-per-grade form.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete repair within the stated architecture is identified. A repair would use a genuinely localised cutoff (e.g. σ(Σψ(x_i)-(d-1))) and reorganise grades so each cube uses an additional hidden layer, e.g. two-layer blocks. The width, per-grade strictness and theorem statement would then have to be re-verified.
issues.overall_effect: For d ≥ 2 the key properties C1-C2, the one-step contraction, pointwise domination, strict L^p decay and the 5d-width single-layer-per-grade realization are not established. The main theorem is unproved for d ≥ 2.
issues.title: The 'cutoff' Ψ is an average of 1-D trapezoids and is not compactly supported for d ≥ 2
issues.why_classification: The central construction fails for all d ≥ 2, and any fix needs deeper per-cube networks. That changes the advertised single-hidden-layer-per-grade architecture and the proof of strict decay at every grade.

issues.failure_explanation: For f ≡ 0 we have M_f = M_{-f} = 0, so T_ε f = T_ε(-f) = 0 and the construction produces no cubes (n = 0), contradicting n ∈ N^+. Property (iii) is impossible for f ≡ 0, since ‖f_2‖_p < ‖f_1‖_p = 0 cannot hold. The iteration in the main proof also needs f_{n_1+1} ≢ 0 at every round, which is never argued. It is true when f ≢ 0 because of the strict pointwise bound at a maximiser, but this is not shown. The cases M_f = 0 or M_{-f} = 0 (one-signed f) are handled only implicitly.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the residual admits an $L^\infty$ contraction by a factor of $1-\varepsilon$.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion and introduction speak of 'strict contraction' at every grade. What is proved is pointwise non-increase |R_{k+1}| ≤ |R_k|, strict decrease of L^p norms, and an L^∞ contraction by 1-ε only over blocks of n_i grades. For the L^∞ norm, the decrease at a single grade is only non-strict, since each grade changes the residual on one small cube. No per-grade contraction factor is established. The related heuristic that every new grade yields 'a substantial error decrease' has no support in the theory.

issues.overall_effect: The qualitative strength of the per-grade guarantee is overstated relative to Theorems thm:main:mgdl and thm:main:mgdl:one:op.
issues.title: Conclusion overstates per-grade contraction
